title: Formula Sheet & Equation Solving Blueprint
objectives: Quickly review transposition rules, cross-multiplication shortcuts, and word problem translation tables

blocks.heading: The 4 Golden Transposition Rules
blocks.content:
| LHS Operation | Moving to RHS becomes | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Addition (+) | Subtraction (-) | $x + 5 = 12 \implies x = 12 - 5$ |
| Subtraction (-) | Addition (+) | $x - 7 = 10 \implies x = 10 + 7$ |
| Multiplication (*) | Division (/) | $4x = 28 \implies x = 28 / 4$ |
| Division (/) | Multiplication (*) | $x / 3 = 9 \implies x = 9 \times 3$ |

blocks.heading: Cross Multiplication Shortcut
blocks.content:
For equations of the form:
$$\frac{ax + b}{cx + d} = \frac{p}{q}$$
Cross multiply diagonally:
$$q(ax + b) = p(cx + d)$$
*Warning:* Remember to distribute $q$ and $p$ to BOTH terms in each binomial!

blocks.heading: English to Algebra Translation Dictionary
blocks.content:
• 'Sum of a number and 7' $\to x + 7$
• 'Difference of a number and 4' $\to x - 4$
• 'Twice a number increased by 5' $\to 2x + 5$
• 'Three consecutive integers' $\to x, x+1, x+2$
• 'Father is 3 times as old as son' $\to F = 3S$

workedExamples.prompt: Translate and solve: The sum of three consecutive multiples of 11 is 363. What is the smallest multiple?
steps: Step 1: Let the three multiples be 11x, 11(x + 1), and 11(x + 2).

takeaways: Always check word problems against real-life sense (e.g. age cannot be negative).
Cross multiplication requires grouping numerators and denominators in brackets.
